featured_reviews.name: Sulabh Sanjay
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited Kerala Café, Vasai after seeing several recommendations on Instagram reels. Being a Malayalee, I was quite eager to try it out. We went in the afternoon and were asked by one of the waiters to wait outside due to crowding. My family and I waited patiently, but after a while, we noticed other groups being seated, eating, and leaving, while we were still waiting outside.When we followed up, we realized that the waiter had completely forgotten about us. Each time we asked, he simply said that the tables were being cleaned, but in reality, other waiting groups were being seated before us. It clearly showed complete mismanagement and a lack of real interest in customer service.The ambience was nice enough, but the food was not as tasty as expected and definitely not worth the hype. The prices were also quite high for the quality offered. To make it worse, there was a lot of noise coming from the kitchen almost as if a fight was going on inside, haha.It seems that the restaurant relies heavily on social media popularity rather than genuine service or taste. Overall, it was a huge disappointment; we ended up waiting for nearly an hour due to their poor management, making it a regrettable experience for me and my family.

This experience is very concerning, and I sincerely apologize for the lack of attention and care you received during your visit. Your feedback will be a catalyst for improving our service standards.
Regards,
Team Kerala Cafe, Vasai

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
True Taste is one of the oldest Mughlai food spots in Vasai, started around 21 years ago since 2005, and it has long been our go-to place for Mughlai cravings. Over the years it has remained a reliable favourite whenever we’re craving hearty, flavourful non-veg food in Vasai.

Despite its simple and unassuming setup, the kitchen consistently delivers food packed with bold spices and comforting flavours. What we personally keep going back for are their Chicken Bhuna with Paratha, which has almost become our default order here. The bhuna gravy is rich, deeply spiced and incredibly satisfying, while the parathas are soft and perfect for scooping up every bit of that delicious curry. Their various chicken and mutton curries are equally comforting and full of character, making them ideal for a proper indulgent Mughlai meal.

Another absolute favourite is their Chicken Baida Roti, which is always a treat — crisp on the outside, packed with flavourful filling and extremely satisfying. For quick bites, the Chicken Shawarma is also very popular and makes for a great grab-and-go option.

The menu has plenty of other delicious dishes worth exploring. Their Chicken White Tandoori, Chicken Red Tikka, Chicken Seekh Kebab and Mutton Seekh Kebab are great starters if you enjoy smoky tandoori flavours. Rice lovers can go for the Chicken Biryani or Chicken Fried Rice, while local favourites like Mutton Keema Pav and Chicken Bhuna Pav bring in that comforting street-style touch.

And of course, a meal here often ends on a sweet note with their pudding/custard, which is simple, nostalgic and one of our personal favourites.

A special mention has to go to Ramzan time, when the place truly comes alive with a variety of special starters and seasonal dishes that are absolutely worth trying. It’s one of the best times to visit if you want to explore more of what their kitchen has to offer.

What makes True Taste special is the consistency of flavour, generous portions and the comforting familiarity of their food. It’s the kind of neighbourhood place you return to again and again because you know the meal will always hit the spot.

A wonderful spot in Vasai for flavourful Mughlai dishes, shawarmas and comforting curries.

featured_reviews.name: Rashida P
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was a totally "True Waste" experience.
I recently ordered Dabba Gosht and Bheja Fry and was quite disappointed with the quality of both dishes.

The Dabba Gosht contained only few very small pieces of mutton chunks and did not appear to have been cooked in a rich mutton stock as expected. Additionally, despite specifically mentioning in the cooking instructions that the dish should not be spicy, it was loaded with green chillies and was far spicier than requested.

The Bheja Fry was equally disappointing. It tasted more like an Egg Bhurji than a bheja dish, with very little Bheja present and almost no distinct flavour from it. The dish was also excessively oily.

When I called to provide feedback, the response was rather casual. I was informed that Bheja Fry normally contains egg and that Bheja Masala is the dish made only with bheja, which was surprising as this was not mentioned in the menu. Regarding the Dabba Gosht, the person simply informed the chef that a complaint had been received and then ended the conversation by saying that the owner would be informed, as nothing could be done at that point.

As a customer, I expected both better food quality and a more constructive response to my concerns.

The only item I genuinely enjoyed was the Rumali Roti, which was soft, fresh, and very well made. Unfortunately, that was the only highlight of an otherwise disappointing meal.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Neelam E Punjab, located near the Vasai West railway station, on August 24th, 2024. My experience was mixed, leaning more towards the negative side, especially considering it is advertised as a family bar and restaurant.

Ambiance:
The ambiance was average at best. There was water dripping from the AC onto a nearby dining table, which further flowed onto the floor where we were sitting. This made the environment uncomfortable and hazardous. Despite being labeled as a family bar and restaurant, the presence of individual male customers drinking next to family tables made the setting feel less family-friendly.

Food:
We ordered Thread Chicken Crispy as a starter, followed by Butter Chicken Gravy, Dhaba Chicken Gravy with Tandoori Roti for the main course, and Chicken Fried Rice along with Chicken Schezwan Fried Rice. The food was the highlight of the evening. Every dish we tried was delicious, and the kitchen team deserves full marks for their efforts. The portions were generous, and the pricing was reasonable, making it good value for money.

Service:
The service, however, left much to be desired. The restaurant has a different, higher-priced menu for bookings made via the Zomato app, which felt misleading. While the staff was polite, they lacked proper training. We had to request water glasses, which were provided in fewer numbers than needed. The table was also short on forks and spoons.

Incident:
A major downside of our visit was an unpleasant incident involving an individual male customer who had consumed too much alcohol. He became loud and aggressive, shouting at us for no apparent reason. Although the staff intervened, the damage was done, and the mood of our family gathering was ruined. It was unsettling, and the situation could have escalated if not for the staff's intervention, albeit late.

Cleanliness:
The cleanliness was average, and the dining plates had noticeable scratches, which need to be replaced. This added to the overall sense of neglect in the restaurant's upkeep.

Overall Experience:
Despite the tasty food, the negative aspects of our visit overshadowed the positives. I would not recommend this restaurant for family outings, as the environment does not align with what one would expect from a family bar and restaurant. Allowing customers without families into the family section poses a risk and detracts from the family-friendly atmosphere they claim to offer.

Final Thoughts:
Neelam E Punjab has potential, particularly with its excellent kitchen team. However, they need to address the issues I’ve highlighted to truly become a reliable family restaurant in the future.
